en henvendelse.explanation: "En henvendelse" means "an inquiry". It comes from the verb "at henvende sig" (to get in touch). To thank someone for getting in touch, customer service says: "Tak for din henvendelse" (Thank you for contacting us).

en henvisning.explanation: "En henvisning" means "a referral / reference". It comes from the verb "at henvise" (to refer). To say the doctor sends you on: "Lægen skriver en henvisning" (The doctor writes a referral). To say a text points to a source: "Der er en henvisning til kilden nederst" (There is a reference to the source at the bottom).

en herre.explanation: "En herre" means "a gentleman / lord". To mark the men's restroom, a sign says "Herrer" (Men). Men's clothes are "herretøj" (menswear).

en hersker.explanation: "En hersker" means "a ruler", as in a person who governs a country. It comes from the verb "at herske" (to rule). To say someone rules a country: "Han hersker over landet" (He rules over the country).

en hest.explanation: "En hest" means "a horse". To say you ride: "Hun rider på en hest" (She rides a horse). The word is also the first part of "en hestehale" (a ponytail).

en hestehale.explanation: "En hestehale" means "a ponytail". It is built from "hest" (horse) and "hale" (tail). To say you tie your hair up: "Jeg binder håret i en hestehale" (I tie my hair in a ponytail).

en hilsen.explanation: "En hilsen" means "a greeting". To end a letter or email, write "Venlig hilsen" (Kind regards). To pass on hello to someone: "Mange hilsner til din mor" (Best wishes to your mother).

en himmel.explanation: "En himmel" means "a sky". To say what the sky looks like, use the form "himlen" (the sky): "Himlen er grå" (The sky is gray). The word is also in "en himmelseng" (a canopy bed).

en hindbærsnitte.explanation: "En hindbærsnitte" means "a raspberry slice (pastry)". It is built from "hindbær" (raspberry) and "snitte" (slice). In Denmark, bakeries sell it.

en hindring.explanation: "En hindring" means "an obstacle". It comes from the verb "at hindre" (to prevent). To say something stops you, even something you cannot touch: "Frygt kan være en hindring" (Fear can be an obstacle).

en hingst.explanation: "En hingst" means "a stallion". For a female horse, use "en hoppe" (a mare): "Hoppen står på marken" (The mare is standing in the field).

en historie.explanation: "En historie" means "a story / history". To say someone tells a story: "Fortæl en historie" (Tell a story). To talk about the past of a country: "Danmarks historie" (the history of Denmark).

en historiebog.explanation: "En historiebog" means "a history book". It is built from "historie" (history) and "en bog" (a book). The word "historie" also means "story": "en historie om en prins" (a story about a prince).

en historiker.explanation: "En historiker" means "a historian". It comes from "historie" (history). To say someone's job, leave out "en": "Hun er historiker" (She is a historian).

en hjelm.explanation: "En hjelm" means "a helmet". To tell someone to put it on: "Tag din hjelm på" (Put your helmet on).

en hjemmeopgave.explanation: "En hjemmeopgave" means "a homework assignment". It is built from "hjemme" (at home) and "opgave" (task). For the daily homework from school, use "lektier" (homework): "Jeg laver mine lektier" (I do my homework).

en hjemmeside.explanation: "En hjemmeside" means "a website". It is built from "hjemme" (home) and "side" (page). Do not mix up "hjemme" (at home) and "hjem" (toward home): "Jeg er hjemme" (I am at home) and "Jeg går hjem" (I am going home).

en hjemmesko.explanation: "En hjemmesko" means "a slipper". It is built from "hjemme" (at home) and "sko" (shoe). To talk about two slippers: "et par hjemmesko" (a pair of slippers).

en hjemrejse.explanation: "En hjemrejse" means "a return trip". It is built from "hjem" (home) and "rejse" (trip). The word "rejse" is also a verb: "at rejse hjem" (to travel home).

en hjerne.explanation: "En hjerne" means "a brain". To tell someone to think: "Brug hjernen!" (Use your brain!) The word is also the first part of "hjernerystelse" (concussion), literally "brain shaking".

en hjernerystelse.explanation: "En hjernerystelse" means "a concussion". It is built from "hjerne" (brain) and "rystelse" (shaking). To say someone got one: "Han fik en hjernerystelse i går" (He got a concussion yesterday).

en hjort.explanation: "En hjort" means "a deer". For a smaller deer, use "et rådyr" (a roe deer): "Et rådyr står ved skovkanten" (A roe deer is standing at the edge of the forest).

en hobby.explanation: "En hobby" means "a hobby". To ask someone about it: "Hvad er din hobby?" (What is your hobby?)

en hofte.explanation: "En hofte" means "a hip". To say your hip hurts: "Jeg har ondt i hoften" (My hip hurts). To say someone had a hip replacement: "Hun har fået en ny hofte" (She has got a new hip).

en holdbarhedsdato.explanation: "En holdbarhedsdato" means "a best-before date". It is built from "holdbarhed" (shelf life) and "dato" (date). To say the date has passed: "Holdbarhedsdatoen er overskredet" (The best-before date has passed).
